.²1 Without love or affection. {#kaccinnABihato'BAvEH SabdAdiBiramaNgalEH#} <ls>Bhāg. 1. 14. 40</ls>.
.²2 Non-existent.

.²1 Not being or existing, non-existence; {#gato BAvo'BAvam#} <ls>Mk. 1</ls> has disappeared.
.²2 Absence, want, failure; {#sarvezAmapyaBAve tu brAhmaRA rikTaBAginaH#}
 <ls>Ms. 9. 188</ls>; mostly in <ab>comp.</ab>; {#sarvABAve harennfpaH#} <ls n="Ms.">189</ls> in the absence
 of all, failing all; {#toya˚, anna˚, AhAra˚#} <ab>&c.</ab>
.²3 Annihilation, death, destruction; ({#vaco … paTyamuktam#}) {#rAkzasAnAmaBAvAya#}
 {#tvaM vA na pratipadyase#} <ls>Rām. 5. 21. 10</ls> non-entity; {#nABAva upalabDeH#}
 <ls>Ś. B.</ls>; {#kzaRamAtraBavAmaBAvakAle#} <ls>Śi. 20. 64</ls>; <ls>Ki. 18. 10</ls>.
.²4 (In <ab>phil.</ab>) Privation, non-existence, nullity or negation, supposed
 to be the seventh category or {#padArTa#} in the system of Kaṇāda. [Strictly
 speaking {#aBAva#} is not a separate predicament, like {#dravya, guRa#},
 but is only a negative arrangement of those predicaments; all nameable
 things being divided into positive ({#BAva#}) and negative ({#aBAva#}),
 the first division including {#dravya, guRa, karma, sAmAnya, viSeza#}
 and {#samavAya#}; and the second only one {#aBAva#}; <ab>cf.</ab> {#atra saptamasyABAvakaTanAdeva#}
 {#zaRRAM BAvatvaM prAptaM tena BAvatvena pfTagupanyAso na kftaH#} <ls>Muktā.</ls>].
 {#aBAva#} is defined as {#BAvaBinno'BAvaH#} ({#pratiyogijYAnADInavizayatvam#})
 that whose knowledge is dependent on the knowledge of its {#pratiyogI#}.
 It is of two principal kinds {#saMsargABAva#} and {#anyonyABAva#}; the
 first comprising three varieties {#prAgaBAva, praDvaMsABAva#},

 and {#atyantABAva#}.
